findings.title: TOCTOU Race Condition in Authentication/Authorization — Admin Bypass
findings.description: The login endpoint sets session data (including is_admin=True) BEFORE verifying the password. By racing a POST /login for the admin user (with wrong password) against a concurrent GET /admin_panel using the same session token, an attacker can catch the window where is_admin=True is already written to the server-side session but the password check has not yet failed and cleared it. This gives unauthorized admin access and exposes the flag.
findings.evidence:
flag{3d582313-fe30-457d-ac42-193b066d56c0}

Exploit steps:
1. Login as test:test → obtain session token S
2. Concurrently send:
   a. GET /admin_panel (with session S)
   b. POST /login username=admin&password=wrong (with session S)
3. The server temporarily writes is_admin=True to session S before the password check fails
4. The concurrent admin panel request reads is_admin=True and returns the flag

The race window exists because the Flask app sets session['is_admin'] = user.is_admin before calling the password verification function.
findings.tool_used: custom Python race script using concurrent threading

findings.title: TOCTOU Race Condition in Login AuthZ Check - Admin Panel Bypass
findings.description: The login endpoint sets session['is_admin']=True in the server-side session storage BEFORE completing the bcrypt password verification. This creates a ~275ms TOCTOU race window during which concurrent GET /admin_panel requests with the same session token can read the elevated is_admin=True state, bypassing authorization and gaining admin access without knowing the admin password.
findings.evidence:
Flag captured: flag{3d582313-fe30-457d-ac42-193b066d56c0}

Attack chain:
1. Login as test:test (non-admin user) to obtain logged_in=True session
2. Concurrently: POST /login with admin:wrong (using same session token) + GET /admin_panel
3. During bcrypt check (~275ms), session has is_admin=True
4. GET /admin_panel reads is_admin=True before password check reverts it
5. Admin panel returned with flag

Proof: race condition consistently triggered (6/12 attempts succeeded on first batch)
findings.tool_used: custom Python race condition script using threading.Barrier for synchronized request dispatch

findings.title: Nginx Alias Path Traversal - Flag Exposed
findings.description: Nginx is configured with an 'alias' directive for the /admin location that creates an off-by-one path traversal vulnerability. Requesting /admin../ traverses to the parent directory (/var/www/) which has directory listing enabled and contains flag.txt. This is the classic Nginx alias traversal bug where 'location /admin' uses 'alias /var/www/html/admin/' - the missing trailing slash in the location block allows /admin../ to resolve to /var/www/html/admin/../ = /var/www/html/../ = /var/www/ (or similar). The flag file is directly accessible via /admin../flag.txt.
findings.evidence:
GET /admin../flag.txt HTTP/1.1
Host: 172.17.0.1:45765

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 43

flag{9c29301f-3fea-47b5-924d-413607e3db56}
